subtopic: Token Holder Rights vs. Underlying Shareholder Rights
source_evidence: The rights, obligations and benefits received by the token holder of a synthetic tokenized security may differ significantly from those of a traditional owner in the underlying security.
question: Do token holders always have the same rights as holders of the underlying shares?
answer: No. Rights depend on the tokenization model. An issuer-sponsored tokenized security has the same legal rights as a traditional share of the same class, and a custodial token represents an indirect interest with the same rights, obligations, and benefits as a traditional shareholder. A synthetic token may provide different rights and does not give the holder claims or rights against the issuer of the referenced security.
